rect.title: <b>GOSLAWJ211 Criminal Law & Criminal Justice</b><br>Examines moral and legal justifications for criminalisation and punishment.<br>Investigates guiding principles of criminal law and justice, including criminal<br>accountability, guilt, legality and fundamental principles, and applies theory<br>through a simulated legal aid clinic.

<b>GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law</b><br>Introduces rules, institutions and politics of public international law. Covers<br>treaties, the UN, armed conflict, war crimes, refugee protection and climate<br>change. Students analyse cases, debate issues and produce a podcast connecting<br>law to global challenges.

<b>GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law</b><br>Explores constitutional law and state organisation, using a comparative<br>approach. Covers constitutionalism, separation of powers, judicial review,<br>federalism and fundamental rights, and discusses constitution‑making, religious<br>constitutions and constitutional backsliding.

<b>GOSLAWJ311 Principles of Private Law</b><br>Examines principles of property law, tort law, contract law and other fields<br>within private law. Uses comparisons of legal systems in four countries to<br>explore rights and obligations arising from daily interactions.

<b>GOSLAWJ312 Foundations of European Union Law</b><br>Introduces the EU legal order. Studies institutions, framework, citizenship and<br>the internal market using problem‑based exercises and guest lectures.

<b>GOSHIST111 Modern History</b><br>Provides a chronological overview of history from 1815 to the present. Discusses<br>industrialisation, popular sovereignty and national self‑determination,<br>and covers major economic, political and cultural developments including<br>revolutions, world wars and the fall of communism.

<b>GOSHIST112 Histories of Gender</b><br>Explores lives of ordinary people through the lens of gender from the 19th to<br>21st centuries. Uses storytelling across cultural forms; topics include slavery,<br>mid‑20th‑century life, conversion therapy, queer cinema and banned books;<br>engages with projects like Walking With Pride.

<b>GOSHIST211 History of Empires</b><br>Examines the rise and fall of empires and the contested concept of empire.<br>Discusses oppressive and benevolent features of empires, covers key theories on<br>empires and power politics and analyses major historical examples.

<b>GOSHIST213 Ways of War</b><br>Provides a chronological overview of warfare in the Western world from antiquity<br>to the present. Covers weapons, technology, strategy, defence, mercenaries,<br>cavalry, chivalry, Blitzkrieg, guerrilla warfare and nuclear arsenals,<br>illustrating competition for mastery in Western history.

<b>GOSHIST311 Native American Histories</b><br>This course introduces students to Native American history and life from the<br>19th through the 21st century. It argues that power, fear, misogyny, education,<br>genocide, and resilience shape the Indigenous past and present. Topics we<br>explore include the “Stolen Lives” of Indian children forcibly taken from their<br>homes and placed in Indian Boarding Schools from the 1830’s through the 1990’s;<br>Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls in the twenty-first century;<br>and the individual and community forms of cultural resistance and environmental<br>regeneration that connect past with present and future generations. We learn<br>from the Native American scholars and 2Spirit youth that speak to and with the<br>class. Exchange of cultural and intellectual knowledge also happens when we work<br>with Lakota students to address contemporary challenges. Legislation, memoir,<br>novels, and Indigenous children’s stories are central to our studies. So are the<br>analyses of contemporary music and artistic expressions and exhibitions, as well<br>as Hollywood and Indigenous film featuring Native American histories and lives.

<b>GOSHIST312 Researching the "American Century"</b><br>Guides students through the full arc of historical inquiry, from formulating<br>research questions to engaging critically with sources. Emphasises<br>methodological rigour and interdisciplinary thinking and culminates in a<br>substantial research paper.

<b>GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy</b><br>Offers a legal, historical and philosophical approach to human rights. Studies<br>classical and modern philosophers, traces the rise of human rights, examines<br>the US Bill of Rights and the French Declaration, and discusses human rights<br>treaties.

<b>GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy</b><br>Introduces central themes from Western philosophy over 2,500 years. Encourages<br>inquiry into the significance of philosophical issues and their relation to<br>other disciplines and teaches theoretical methods used by philosophers.

<b>GOSPHIL212 Ethics</b><br>Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology,<br>utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the<br>relation between happiness and pleasure. Applies theories to practical issues<br>such as animal rights, privacy, future generations, war, punishment, disability<br>and equality.

<b>GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind</b><br>Examines historical and modern work on the philosophy of mind. Discusses<br>Descartes’ dualism, the nature of consciousness, AI and animal minds, personal<br>identity, transformative experiences and the influence of technology on<br>experience.

<b>GOSPHIL311 Philosophy of Emotion</b><br>Explores emotions from a philosophical perspective. Discusses nature and<br>rationality of emotions, their role in ethics and art, and draws on historical<br>and contemporary sources.

<b>GOSPHIL313 Free Will, Time & the Self</b><br>Investigates concepts of free will, the role of luck and openness of the future.<br>Explores relations between free will, time and the self across multiple modules<br>and contemporary debates.

<b>GOSPOLI111 Introduction to Political Philosophy</b><br>Introduces political philosophy. Examines concepts such as authority, freedom,<br>equality, democracy, human rights, pluralism, multiculturalism, poverty and<br>environmental issues through classical and contemporary texts. Emphasises essay<br>writing and presentations.

<b>GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics</b><br>Provides analytical tools to compare political systems and democracies. Examines<br>phenomena like democratic backsliding, decline of political parties, rise of<br>populism, media changes, non‑majoritarian institutions and globalization’s<br>impact on domestic politics.

<b>GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations</b><br>Introduces basic theories of international relations and applies them to<br>contemporary issues such as climate change, energy, humanitarian intervention,<br>global crises and international relations between North-South and South-South<br>actors. Includes a UN Security Council negotiation simulation.

<b>GOSPOLI311 European Union Politics</b><br>Introduces EU politics. Outlines actors, institutions and decision‑making<br>rules; examines responses to crises; and employs various approaches to study EU<br>politics and policy‑making.

<b>GOSPOLI312 Public Policy Analysis</b><br>Investigates public policy in the context of globalization. Uses a case study on<br>sugar to examine policy‑making phases and alternative conceptualisations across<br>national and international arenas. Students write policy memos.

<b>GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict</b><br>Introduces Peace & Conflict Studies. Examines definitions of peace and conflict;<br>analyzes conflict causation, violence typologies and radicalisation; applies<br>reconciliation and conflict‑transformation models to real‑world scenarios<br>through lectures and portfolio work.

<b>GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology</b><br>Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines<br>socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois,<br>and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class<br>through theoretical approaches and methodologies.

<b>GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology</b><br>Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions,<br>interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on<br>complexity and power dynamics in social research.

<b>GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology</b><br>Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and<br>colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity<br>and critically engages with sociological discourses.

<b>GOSSOCI215 Social Movements & Environmental Justice</b><br>Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case<br>studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such<br>as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to<br>encourage civic engagement.

<b>GOSSOCI311 New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory</b><br>Examines contemporary sociological debates about civil society through critical<br>tradition, neo‑functionalism and decolonial critiques. Includes research group<br>projects with NGOs or civil society organizations that translate conceptual<br>insights into empirical analysis.

<b>GOSGATE102 Law, Society & Justice</b><br>Examines law from legal, socio‑scientific and normative perspectives. Explores<br>definitions, legal traditions and fields of law, investigates the relationship<br>between law and society and the concept of justice, and includes case law,<br>excursion to international legal organisations, interviews with practitioners<br>and a moot court session.
